Mike / Aditya — attaching the technical notes and a worked example (proforma_proration_example.xlsx will be included in the reissue). Summary below.

Why you saw a blended rate: the March invoice rolled together usage from customers' requests routed to multiple EU regions. Our billing pipeline currently aggregates token/usage charges and applies a blended VAT presentation for compactness. That presentation is confusing for compliance — we'll stop doing that for multi-jurisdiction customers.

How we prorate credits (algorithm):
- Step A: compute taxable base per country = sum of taxable usage tokens originating from that country for the billing period.
- Step B: compute country share = taxable base per country / total taxable base across all countries.
- Step C: allocate credits = total credit amount * country share.
- Step D: per-country VAT = (taxable base per country - allocated credit) * country VAT rate.

Example (simplified):
- Total taxable base = €100,000 (DE €60k, FR €40k)
- Upstream credit = €10,000
- Allocated credits: DE €6,000, FR €4,000
- Taxable bases after credit: DE €54,000, FR €36,000
- If DE VAT=19% and FR VAT=20% then DE VAT=€10,260, FR VAT=€7,200

VAT ID validation: we validate VAT IDs against VIES (EU) and keep a time-stamped snapshot of the check (response code + timestamp). We can provide the validation response for each VAT ID you list. If a VAT ID was validated as "valid" at the time of the invoice and the supply is B2B, reverse-charge applies and we will set the VAT lines to zero-rate with a reverse-charge note. If a VAT ID fails validation, the local VAT rate is applied and we'll flag it for remediation.

Action items (we'll take):

- We'll attach VIES response snapshots for the VAT IDs you confirm.
- We'll include the proforma example file so your tax folks can reproduce the calculations.
